firstWeek: Set up a quiet room with hiding and scratching places. Keep food, water and litter in separate spots.
Let the cat come out on their own schedule. Do not force interaction.
Keep the same food at first. Change foods slowly over 7 to 10 days.
Book a vet check in the first week and bring any health records.
Introduce other pets slowly, with scent swapping before sight.
proofing: Remove lilies and other toxic plants.
Secure windows and balcony doors with sturdy mesh or screens.
Store medicines, cleaning products and string or hair ties out of reach.
Check washers, dryers and recliners before using them.
wish: One litter tray per cat plus one extra, scooped daily, in a quiet spot away from food.
Wet food or added water helps hydration. Cats often drink little from bowls.
Offer short play sessions. Stop when the cat tires. Let the cat catch the toy, then put string toys away.
Brush teeth with a toothpaste made for cats. Start slowly and keep it positive.
Take a photo and weigh your cat monthly, so changes are easy to spot.
